CLINICAL EVIDENCE

Research you can examine.

Four supplied publications, with their findings and limits. Assessment evidence is kept separate from home rehabilitation claims.

VR EYE-TRACKING ASSESSMENT
npj Digital Medicine · 2024 · 7:219

A portable and efficient dementia screening tool using eye tracking machine learning and virtual reality

Xu Y, Zhang C, Pan B, Yuan Q, Zhang X

201 participantsMoCA correlation r = 0.90; sensitivity 88.5%; specificity 83%

VECA combined VR eye tracking with machine learning to estimate MoCA scores and classify cognitive impairment. The study used five-fold cross-validation.

Applicability & limitations

Scope: VR eye-tracking assessment research; the paper includes Shenzhen Yiwei Technology affiliations. Commercial-model equivalence needs documentation.

Limitations: Shenzhen cohort; no cross-center training/testing. Screening agreement does not establish home-training benefit, disease prevention or diagnostic certainty.

Publisher articleSupplied PDF
VR EYE-TRACKING ASSESSMENT
Chinese Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging · 2024 · 15(6):49–53

Application value of structural MRI combined with computerized cognitive assessment based on VR eye-tracking technology in early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease

Wei Z et al.

135 participants · 77 early AD / 58 cognitively unimpairedCombined AUC 0.825 vs hippocampal-volume-only AUC 0.629

A five-minute VR eye-tracking assessment was studied alongside structural MRI. Adding the assessment score improved discrimination compared with hippocampal volume alone (P < 0.001).

Applicability & limitations

Scope: Clinical assessment plus imaging; not a home rehabilitation trial.

Limitations: Single-site clinical sample. The combined result requires MRI and must not be attributed to the headset alone.

RELATED ASSESSMENT RESEARCH
BMC Public Health · 2024 · 24:1206

Community screening for dementia among older adults in China: a machine learning-based strategy

Zhang Y et al.

823 adults aged 65 years and olderMLP AUC 0.83 ± 0.04 vs AD8 baseline AUC 0.65

Machine-learning models combined selected AD8 questions with health characteristics in the SHARE community cohort.

Applicability & limitations

Scope: Related community-screening methodology. This study did not test a VR device or demonstrate QuickMind efficacy.

Limitations: Performance relates to this cohort, selected health features and the study reference assessment; it is not a VR product performance claim.

Publisher articleSupplied PDF
RELATED ASSESSMENT RESEARCH
American Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease & Other Dementias · 2024 · 39

Development and Validation of an Automatic Computerized Neurocognitive Battery in Chinese

Zhang J, Hong Z, Yang L, Li X, Ye F

86 volunteers · ages 51–82Manual/system scoring correlation 0.904–1.0

The CNBC provided automated testing and scoring. Correlations with paired paper-based measures ranged from 0.256 to 0.666.

Applicability & limitations

Scope: Related computerized-assessment validation. It is not a VR rehabilitation study; supplied material does not establish QuickMind product equivalence.

Limitations: Preliminary Chinese-speaking volunteer sample; score agreement is not treatment efficacy or diagnostic accuracy.

Publisher articleSupplied PDF
These studies investigate assessment or screening. They do not establish the treatment efficacy, prevention benefit or regulatory status of the proposed QuickMind Home Plan.
